implementation_notes: ScalaMock is the native Scala framework documented by ScalaTest: mock[]/mockFunction create doubles, expectations are declared with expects ... returns (optionally repeated n times), and verification can also run after the fact with (collaborator.someMethod _).verify(args).once(). What replaces the classic spy object is the generated mock plus the verify DSL; proxy (dynamic) and generated (type-safe) mock styles trade runtime flexibility for compile-time checking.
code_sketch:
val mailer = mock[Mailer]                       // in a MockFactory suite
new OrderService(mailer).place(order)
(mailer.send _).verify("bob@example.com", body).once()
pitfalls: Function-mock syntax needs the eta-expanded form (mailer.send _); passing the method directly creates a new function object that verifies nothing.
Generated (type-safe) mocks rely on macros; in mixed Java/Scala builds the ScalaTest guide suggests Mockito so one framework serves both languages.

variants.name: Mockito-Scala spy (Java Mockito API, Scala syntax)
variants.implementation_notes: Mockito-Scala re-exports Mockito's spy through Scala-friendly syntax: spy / verify calls, the `was called` and experimental expect DSLs, argumentCaptor[T] capture, and spyLambda[T] for spying lambdas, which plain spy cannot wrap because the compiler emits them as final classes. What replaces the classic spy object is Mockito's JVM proxy plus the Scala DSL; it is also the recommended route when the suite already uses Java mocking frameworks.
variants.code_sketch:
val mailer = spy[Mailer]                      // or spy(new Mailer)
new OrderService(mailer).place(order)
verify(mailer).send(eqTo("bob@example.com"), any)
val captor = argumentCaptor[String]
verify(mailer).send(any, captor.capture())
captor.value should include(order.id)
pitfalls: The idiomatic `aMock.bar(*) was called` syntax and the experimental expect DSL differ in semantics; mixing the two styles in one suite invites order-sensitive mistakes.
Spying on a lambda requires spyLambda[T] - a plain spy of a val lambda spies the value, not the code, because the compiler turns lambdas into final classes.
